cohort: The study included women who underwent LSCS in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology of a specific hospital over a 14-month period.
finding: The institutional LSCS prevalence was 44.94%, with the most common indications being previous LSCS (42%) and failure of induction of labor (25%).
mod_finding: The study found an LSCS prevalence of 44.94%, identifying previous LSCS (42%) as the leading indication and failure of induction of labor (25%) as the second most common reason for this mode of birth.
gest_age: 5% of LSCS occurred at <32 weeks, 25% between 32-36 weeks, and 70% between 37-40 weeks of gestation.
